facts.text: Magnolia Township was organized in 1872, named by settler Philo Hawes after his Wisconsin hometown of Magnolia.
After being platted in 1891, Magnolia officially incorporated as a town in 1894, marking its first formal municipal status.
Paul Railway expanded in 1884 and opened a new station in 1886, turning Magnolia into a grain shipping hub.
Magnolia exhibits a humid continental climate (Köppen Dfa), featuring pronounced seasonal variations with frigid winters and warm summers influenced by its location in the Great Plains.
Southwestern Minnesota Plains expose Magnolia to frequent thunderstorms and a moderate tornado risk each spring and summer, part of Tornado Alley.
Magnolia’s post office opened in 1886, serving the community for over a century of mail delivery.
